patterns.what_worked: Modelling the failing client instead of the intended one: the new suite makes CheckInteractDistance a recording thrower and loads the real vendored LibRangeCheck as shipped, so the zero-call pin and the empty-list getRange pin are executable, not static-only. Splitting the LRC flag in two (lrc_unavailable = init deadline for /st diag, rf_disabled = poll dead-man) kept the diag line truthful without making range state depend on the library. The mutation run (9/9, each failing on a named check, byte-identical restores) proved every new guard and boundary is load-bearing.
patterns.what_was_hard: The harness moved under the lane: a first run failed 2/44 on crossfire owned by the compat lane (secret_guard_state still pinned the removed api.CheckInteractDistance; toc_check lacked the two new suite registrations), and by landing time both were resolved externally (46/46 green, secret_guard_state rewritten to assert the wrapper is absent at 432 checks). Also the first mutation draft silently failed to apply M6/M7/M9 because multi-line old strings used LF against CRLF files; the CRLF-aware Python runner replaced it so those mutants actually mutated.
patterns.skill_gap: No client was loaded, so the protected-call removal and the helper's live show/hide remain UNCONFIRMED until the operator runs the §8 checklist. The 10 yd sweet-spot band is sourced from the brief's statement about the reference's index-3 band; the reference addon source is not in this repo, so its exact file:line is not independently verified.
